records.name: Traps
records.description: The SRD 5.2 Gameplay Toolbox (p. 199) describes how to present traps (severity and levels, trigger, effect) and advises using them sparingly. It does not include the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide Appendix A random dungeon generation tables, which are not part of the SRD.

parts.name: Severity and Levels
parts.description: A trap is designated as a nuisance or as deadly for characters of certain levels. A nuisance trap is unlikely to seriously harm characters of the indicated levels, whereas a deadly trap can grievously damage characters of the indicated levels.

parts.name: Trigger
parts.description: Traps are often set to go off when a creature enters an area or touches an object. Examples include stepping on a pressure plate, crossing a trip wire, turning a doorknob, or using the wrong key in a lock.

records.name: Collapsing Roof
records.trigger: A creature crosses a trip wire
records.description: A trip wire 3 inches off the ground topples two weak supports and brings down an unstable section of ceiling. Each creature beneath it makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
records.avoid: Once detected, the trip wire can be easily cut or avoided (no ability check required).

records.name: Falling Net
records.trigger: A creature crosses a trip wire
records.description: A trip wire releases a weighted 10-foot-square Net on the first creature to cross it. The target must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or have the Restrained condition until it escapes (Huge or larger succeeds automatically); an action and a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check frees a creature within reach.
records.avoid: Once detected, the trip wire can be easily cut or avoided (no ability check required).

records.name: Fire-Casting Statue
records.trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
records.duration: Instantaneous, and the trap resets at the start of the next turn
records.description: A nearby statue exhales a 15-foot Cone of magical flame. Each creature in the Cone makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. A DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check finds a glyph on the statue (defacing it disarms the trap); a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check finds the pressure plate (an Iron Spike under it stops the trap).
records.avoid: Wedging an Iron Spike or similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

records.name: Hidden Pit
records.trigger: A creature moves onto the pit's lid
records.description: A 10-foot-deep pit under a hinged lid that matches the floor. A creature that moves onto the lid falls in and takes 3 (1d6) Bludgeoning damage. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check detects it; an Iron Spike wedged under the lid makes it safe to cross.
records.avoid: An Iron Spike or similar object wedged between the lid and the floor keeps the lid from opening.

records.name: Poisoned Darts
records.trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
records.duration: Instantaneous, and the trap resets at the start of the next turn if it has activated fewer than three times
records.description: Poisoned darts shoot from hidden tubes in the walls. Each creature in their path makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or is struck by 1d3 darts, taking 3 (1d6) Poison damage per dart. A DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check finds the holes or the pressure plate.
records.avoid: Plugging the holes, or wedging an Iron Spike under the pressure plate, prevents the darts from firing.

records.name: Poisoned Needle
records.trigger: A creature opens the trap's lock improperly or fails to disarm the trap
records.description: A needle hidden in a lock stabs whoever opens it without the proper key: DC 11 Constitution saving throw, 5 (1d10) Poison damage and the Poisoned condition for 1 hour on a failure, half damage only on a success. A DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check finds the needle; a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check disarms it, and a failed check triggers it.
records.avoid: The trap doesn't trigger if the lock is opened with a Knock spell or similar magic.

records.name: Rolling Stone
records.trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
records.description: Deadly Trap (Levels 11-16) or Nuisance Trap (Levels 17-20). A 5-foot-radius orb of stone rolls 60 feet a turn; a creature whose space it enters makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or takes 55 (10d10) Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check deduces the pressure plate's function; an Iron Spike under it stops the trap.
records.avoid: Wedging an Iron Spike or a similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

records.name: Spiked Pit
records.trigger: A creature moves onto the pit's lid
records.description: A 10-foot-deep pit with spikes at the bottom under a hinged lid. A creature that falls in takes 3 (1d6) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 (2d8) Piercing damage. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check detects it; an Iron Spike wedged under the lid makes it safe to cross.
records.avoid: An Iron Spike or similar object wedged between the lid and the floor keeps the lid from opening.
